issues.description: Hardcoded utterance counts complect data identity with verification logic
issues.detail: The here-doc in local/data.sh embeds magic numbers (22467, 3208, 6072, 29386, 38924) tied to a specific snapshot of the dataset. Counts are a value (a fact about that snapshot), but they are inlined into the script that prepares the data. If TAL re-releases, the script fails opaquely. Pull the expected counts out as data (a manifest file) or compute them from the transcripts.

issues.description: download_and_untar.sh swallows the 'unzip missing' error and continues
issues.detail: The unzip check echoes a message but does not exit. The script then proceeds and the first unzip call fails far from the real cause. This complects 'tool available' with 'tool runs' silently. Either exit non-zero when unzip is absent or stop pretending to check. The simple version is one early exit, not a warning that the rest of the script ignores.

issues.description: Usage block prints but does not exit, hiding argument errors
issues.detail: When the wrong number of arguments is passed, the script prints usage and then continues into realpath with possibly empty $1. That is place-oriented thinking: the program limps on with bad state. Add 'exit 1' after the usage block so a misuse is a value the caller can observe immediately, not a downstream crash.

issues.description: Transcript normalization is a chain of seds that complects rule and mechanism
issues.detail: The pipeline of seven sed substitutions to strip punctuation and full-width characters is incidental complexity inline in the prep script. The set of characters to normalize is a value; the substitution is a function. Lift the character map into a small table (file or array) so future Mandarin recipes can reuse it and additions do not require editing a pipe chain.

issues.description: README links to a config path that does not exist in the diff
issues.detail: The README points ASR config at ./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml but the file is actually ./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml. Small, but it is a fact-about-the-world that disagrees with the world. Either move the file or fix the link so the document is a true value.

review.summary: This is a recipe addition that mostly follows the ESPnet template, so most of the code is rightly delegated to symlinks. The complecting that remains is in local/data.sh and local/download_and_untar.sh, where dataset facts (file counts, character normalization rules) are inlined into the procedural script rather than expressed as data the script consumes. The download script also has two control-flow holes (missing-unzip and bad-args paths) that let bad state propagate — classic place-oriented bugs. Nothing is structurally wrong; the question that should have been asked first is "what is a value here and what is a procedure?" — the answer would have cleaned up about half the script.
